```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

UCDP data expose more than one form of uncertainty. Event records include
spatial and temporal precision codes, while successive releases may revise
previously published observations. `ucdpR` makes both dimensions inspectable
without converting them into a single substantive uncertainty measure.

```{r}
library(ucdpR)

events <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021, 2021, 2021),
  where_prec = c(1, 2, 3, 6, NA),
  date_prec = c(1, 2, 4, 5, 1),
  best = c(4, 8, 2, 12, 1)
)
```

## Precision as reported uncertainty

Begin by showing the distribution rather than immediately discarding less
precise observations.

```{r}
ucdp_precision(events)
ucdp_precision(events, by = "year")
```

An analysis can then define transparent thresholds and compare results across
them.

```{r}
strict_sample <- ucdp_filter_precision(
  events, where_prec = 1, date_prec = 1:2
)

broader_sample <- ucdp_filter_precision(
  events, where_prec = 1:3, date_prec = 1:4
)

nrow(strict_sample)
nrow(broader_sample)
```

## Revisions between releases

The comparison function accepts preloaded data frames, which makes the core
operation reproducible and easy to demonstrate without downloading data.

```{r}
old <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4,
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021, 2021),
  best = c(4, 8, 2, 12),
  where_prec = c(1, 2, 3, 6),
  version = "24.1"
)

new <- data.frame(
  id = 2:5,
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2021, 2021),
  best = c(8, 3, 12, 1),
  where_prec = c(2, 2, 6, 1),
  version = "25.1"
)

comparison <- ucdp_compare_versions(
  "ged",
  old_version = "24.1",
  new_version = "25.1",
  key = "id",
  old_data = old,
  new_data = new
)

comparison$overview
comparison$variables
comparison$added
comparison$removed
comparison$modified
```

Cell-level output is useful when the direction and magnitude of individual
changes matter.

```{r}
cell_comparison <- ucdp_compare_versions(
  "ged", "24.1", "25.1",
  key = "id", old_data = old, new_data = new,
  detail = "cells"
)
cell_comparison$cell_changes
```

For official releases, omit `old_data` and `new_data` and supply exact version
identifiers:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
official_comparison <- ucdp_compare_versions(
  "ged", old_version = "24.1", new_version = "25.1"
)
```

Revision frequency is not automatically measurement error: changes may reflect
new information, corrected coding, altered definitions, or expanded coverage.
The comparison identifies what changed; substantive interpretation still
requires the relevant codebooks and version histories.

Direct integration with `uncertainUCDP` will be documented after its current
API and the meaning of the exchanged objects have been verified. Until then,
the outputs remain ordinary tibbles that can be inspected or transformed by
downstream uncertainty workflows without an undocumented dependency.
